text:
Buffalo arrives winless in three (0-1-2), all of it in overtime or a shootout, and the latest sting came three days ago in Washington, where the Sabres blew a two-goal lead and lost 4-3. They're missing Jiri Kulich, Sam Carrick and Matt Grzelcyk. San Jose lost 6-4 at Boston in a game that included Casey Mittelstadt's 100th career goal, and the Sharks are without Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov. Collin Graf has stepped into both spots and is up to 17:02 a night.

Our numbers favor Buffalo here (3.46 expected goals to 2.98). At five on five, the Sabres have taken 51% of the expected goals, which measure chance quality, while the Sharks sit at 44% and allow 4.01 per 60 minutes. Buffalo is better than its record, with finishing and goaltending costing it. San Jose takes 4.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Colten Ellis (+0.16 goals saved above expected this season) and Yaroslav Askarov (+3.85) are both off small samples. Askarov was at -19.4 last season, Ellis at +2.18.

Tage Thompson is 40% to score and Jack Quinn 33% on a four-game point streak. For San Jose, Macklin Celebrini is 43% to score and 82% for a point; Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest posted that he's "skating like a madman." Our under-the-radar pick is Owen Power, 54% for a point against a team giving up the second-most chances in the league.
